title: HADES vs PLAIN STACK ordinary explanation and follow-up probe after user-only routing fixes
status: exploratory matched direct-agent probe; no owner preference
supersedes: hades-core-local-explanation-followup-pair-v1.json as the post-routing-fix sample; v1 remains the pre-fix comparison

conditions.hermes: 0.21.5, source commit f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f, same candidate venv
conditions.ollama: 0.35.1 staged official archive SHA-256 9fcd79ac4575b2bd31b992eee18b1000c8ad126b451627c8f8cd091714cfbb10 at loopback port 11445
conditions.hardware: same local RTX 3080 Ti laptop; staged inference host, model stayed loaded during measured sample
conditions.runtime_context: Ollama server log reported n_ctx_slot=4096; both stacks used same staged runtime/model/context behavior
conditions.reasoning: reasoning_config={"enabled":false}; direct Hermes agent constructor, max_tokens=512
conditions.tools: Hermes AIAgent enabled_toolsets=[] on both stacks; no tools exposed or called (empty schema serialized as 2 bytes)
conditions.measurement: one AIAgent run per process/turn; streaming callback first nonempty delta for TTFT; timer excludes Python/Hermes import and AIAgent construction, includes run_conversation and HADES routing. One model API call per request. Conversation history preserved independently for each stack. Actual aggregate request message character totals are recorded per turn.
conditions.order_and_warmup: Per-case stack order alternated. Each profile received one "Hi." warm-up, but the HADES warm-up took 59,778.2ms while PLAIN took 1,231.2ms, indicating asymmetric cold/model-prefix state; both warm-ups are excluded. First measured conversation turn per stack is also excluded from warm medians. Remaining turns are paired and stack order alternates, though model batching/cache cannot be fully controlled.

interpretation.observation: After commits 75ca0401 and 9238e960, no assistant-generated text or ambiguous research follow-up activated an unrelated tool path in this ordinary subset: all ten measured turns exposed/called zero tools and used one model generation. HADES warm median TTFT remained higher by 526.4ms; warm median wall was 171.3ms lower, with a notably longer HADES "Examples?" response. The subset does not isolate the cause of TTFT and is too small for broad product or preference claims.

limitations: Five synthetic prompts only; no natural owner dogfood or blind preference scoring.
Direct AIAgent calls omit Open WebUI, live API gateway, Hindsight recall, domain services, and production process startup.
The model/runtime/hardware are staged and differ from production; production model digest is not matched.
The HADES warm-up was cold/asymmetric and is reported but excluded; first conversation turn per stack is excluded from warm medians.
No exposed tools means this measures ordinary explanation/follow-up behavior, not real domain-tool activation.
Latency is end-to-end within run_conversation; routing, prompt construction, provider prefill, and model scheduling were not separated.
